domain: anniversary dinner at an Italian trattoria
base_instruction: You are a helpful dining and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan their anniversary dinner at an Italian trattoria by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, my wife and I are celebrating our 10th anniversary this Friday and we're thinking of going to that Italian trattoria downtown. Can you help us plan?

flow_info.value: Four people: me, my wife Sarah, my buddy Marco, and Marco's partner Diane
Marco grew up in Naples, his family is from there
Diane was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Budget is around 80 dollars per person, it's a special occasion but we don't want to go crazy
Marco's sister Elena is in town visiting and he wants to bring her along, so that's five now
Elena had a bad reaction to pine nuts at a dinner party a couple years ago, had to use an EpiPen
Diane just texted Marco — she caught a stomach bug and can't make it. She feels terrible about missing it
Sarah just got back from her OB appointment — turns out she has gestational diabetes now, so she needs to watch her sugar intake on top of everything else
Menu items to check: classic pesto genovese pasta, beef carpaccio, eggplant parmigiana, tiramisu, mushroom risotto, Caesar salad

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or undercooked meat, raw fish, unpasteurized cheese, high-mercury fish, raw eggs
inference_chain: Pregnant → must avoid raw/undercooked meat and fish

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Diane was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
No wheat pasta, no regular bread, no flour-based sauces

constraints.value: Allergic to pine nuts specifically (tree nut allergy — pine nuts), not all nuts
constraints.surface_form: Elena had a bad reaction to pine nuts at a dinner party a couple years ago, had to use an EpiPen

constraints.value: Must limit sugar intake — avoid high-sugar desserts and heavily sweetened dishes
constraints.surface_form: Sarah just got back from her OB appointment — turns out she has gestational diabetes now, so she needs to watch her sugar intake on top of everything else

hidden_state.value: You are planning a 10th anniversary dinner at an Italian trattoria for yourself, your wife Sarah, and friends. The guest list will change: Marco's sister Elena joins, Diane drops out. Sarah's dietary constraints will expand (gestational diabetes added to pregnancy). At the end you will present a list of menu items and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at what the problems might be — just ask openly.

You are a calm, upbeat person excited about your anniversary dinner. You relay updates about other people in third person (e.g. 'Marco told me...', 'Sarah just got back from...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal social coordination among friends.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: pesto genovese contains pine nuts (Elena's allergy); beef carpaccio is raw meat (Sarah pregnant — cannot eat raw meat); tiramisu contains raw eggs and high sugar (Sarah pregnant — raw eggs, and gestational diabetes — sugar); Caesar salad traditionally has raw egg in dressing (Sarah pregnant). Agent confirms eggplant parmigiana and mushroom risotto are fine. Agent does NOT flag gluten as a problem (Diane is no longer coming).
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Of the six items: (1) Classic pesto genovese pasta contains pine nuts — Elena had a severe allergic reaction to pine nuts requiring an EpiPen, so this is dangerous for her. This is the hidden ingredient trap: pesto looks like a simple herb sauce but traditional pesto genovese is made with pine nuts. (2) Beef carpaccio is raw beef — Sarah is 5 months pregnant and cannot eat raw or undercooked meat. (3) Tiramisu traditionally contains raw eggs (in the mascarpone/sabayon layer) — problematic for Sarah's pregnancy; additionally, tiramisu is a high-sugar dessert, problematic for Sarah's gestational diabetes. (4) Caesar salad traditionally has raw egg in the dressing — problematic for Sarah's pregnancy. (5) Eggplant parmigiana is fine for everyone currently attending. (6) Mushroom risotto is fine for everyone currently attending. Diane's celiac/gluten constraint no longer applies because she is not coming.
required_elements: Pesto genovese pasta is problematic: traditional pesto genovese contains pine nuts, which Elena is severely allergic to (EpiPen reaction)
Beef carpaccio is problematic: it is raw beef, and Sarah is pregnant — pregnant women should not eat raw or undercooked meat
Tiramisu is problematic for Sarah on two counts: traditional tiramisu contains raw eggs (pregnancy risk) and it is a high-sugar dessert (gestational diabetes)
Caesar salad is problematic: traditional Caesar dressing contains raw egg, which is unsafe for Sarah's pregnancy
Eggplant parmigiana is fine for everyone currently attending
Mushroom risotto is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish for gluten or celiac concerns (Diane is no longer coming, her constraint is removed)
Flagging pesto as problematic for anyone other than Elena (pine nut allergy is Elena's constraint specifically)
Saying Elena has a general nut allergy or tree nut allergy beyond pine nuts (she specifically reacted to pine nuts)
Flagging eggplant parmigiana as problematic for any current diner
Flagging mushroom risotto as problematic for any current diner
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 turns. Key tracking challenges: (1) Sarah is pregnant → agent must infer no raw meat, no raw eggs, no unpasteurized cheese (inferential chain, pregnancy dietary rules). (2) Diane has celiac disease → gluten constraint, but Diane EXITS mid-conversation, so gluten is no longer a concern at probe time. This is the removed-entity trap: models often keep flagging gluten for pasta and risotto even after Diane drops out. (3) Elena joins late (Turn 3) with a pine nut allergy — the hidden ingredient trap: classic pesto genovese is made with pine nuts, but many people think of pesto as just basil and olive oil. The agent must know pesto's traditional recipe includes pine nuts. (4) Sarah's constraint is UPGRADED in Turn 6 with gestational diabetes (low sugar), adding a second dimension to her restrictions. Tiramisu fails on both raw eggs (pregnancy) and high sugar (gestational diabetes). (5) Caesar salad is a subtler trap — traditional Caesar dressing uses raw egg yolk, which is unsafe during pregnancy. The agent must catch this non-obvious ingredient. (6) Eggplant parmigiana and mushroom risotto are clearly fine for all current diners — the agent should confirm these without false flags.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
